summary.text: A 10-year-old girl presented to the outpatient department with hi-grade fever, headache and pain around the left half of the face. She had a history of left ear discharge since the age of two that was treated conservatively. She was febrile and toxic, with a huge tender fluctuant swelling in the left temporal and occipital region crossing the midline.

Examination showed left chronic suppurative otitis media of the attico-antral type with cholesteatoma and a foul smelling discharge, a normal right ear, no meningeal irritation and a normal fundus. Hemoglobin was 8.2 g/dl, leukocytes 22300/mm3 with 88% neutrophils, and ESR 48 mm in the first hour. Audiometry showed severe left conductive hearing loss, and HRCT showed a soft tissue mass in the mastoid antrum and middle ear with erosion of the mastoid tip, reported as Citelli’s abscess.

After complete evaluation the abscess was drained under general anesthesia through a postaural incision, and her general condition improved significantly. After 3 weeks of parenteral antibiotic therapy, a left modified radical mastoidectomy with middle temporal artery based flap obliteration of cavity was performed.
